_comment: Fixed sample graph for the grounded-triple-checker worked scenario: a fictional video-encoding and streaming company, Cobalt Stream. This is NOT a schema/shape template (read-path kits don't ship schema.example.json) -- it is a small, already-populated, ready-to-query graph standing in for a much larger production graph (a real one might carry thousands of change/module edges; this file holds 10 nodes so the whole thing is easy to read while the checker demonstrates that its verdict on each claim came from a single edge in this file, never from anything written in the change's own description). 'change' nodes are connected to 'module' nodes by 'touches' edges; every one of them was pulled straight out of an actual diff by extraction, never guessed at from summarizing what the change's author wrote about it. 'claim' nodes record a change/module pair someone asserted is NOT connected by a 'touches' edge, and are linked to the change they were made about by a 'claims' edge. Nothing in this file marks which claim is true -- that is exactly what check-claim and graph-verifier have to work out from the 'touches' edges alone.

nodes.description: Batches duplicate thumbnail-regeneration requests together and merges the CDN purge calls they trigger, cutting redundant work in the encoding pipeline's asset-refresh path. Its own description claims it does not touch drm-license-issuer.

Adds a retry ceiling to the subtitle-sync worker so a flaky captioning vendor can't spin it in a loop, and swaps in a cache helper pulled from the license module to skip a duplicate lookup. Reads like a small subtitle-timing fix; its own description also claims it does not touch drm-license-issuer.

Rewrites the metrics exporter's histogram bucket boundaries so latency percentiles bucket more finely. Has no claim attached and no connection to the license issuer or subtitle pipeline -- included to show a change that never enters either claim's verdict.
Generates thumbnail images for uploaded video assets.
Issues CDN cache-purge calls whenever an asset changes.
Synchronizes subtitle tracks against a video's audio timeline; calls out to a third-party captioning vendor.

Issues and revokes DRM playback licenses for protected video assets. The sensitive module both of this kit's claims are about -- a change reaching into it needs to be visible even when its own description never mentions doing so.
Exports internal pipeline metrics to the monitoring stack. Part of an unrelated cluster neither claim in this kit ever references.
